mainTopic: Who must move away when neighbors' things harm each other: על המזיק or על הניזק, in the מחלוקת between רבנן and רבי יוסי
overview: The משנה teaches that a person must keep harmful things away from a neighbor's property: משרה (flax-soaking water) away from ירק, and חרדל away from bees. רבי יוסי disagrees about חרדל. The גמרא asks how such things could end up at the border at all, and רב פפא answers that the case is a לוקח, someone who bought land where the items were already in place. רבינא explains that the רבנן still make the buyer move, because על המזיק להרחיק את עצמו: the one causing harm must distance himself. The גמרא first suggests that רבי יוסי also holds על המזיק and argues only because mustard and bees harm each other. The רבנן answer that bees do not really harm mustard. Then a משנה about a pit and a tree shows that רבי יוסי holds על הניזק. So the גמרא concludes that his mustard argument was only made 'according to your view' against the רבנן. The amud ends as the רבנן begin their reply again, and that reply continues on the next amud.

steps.title: How can the harmful items end up at the border?
steps.stepSummary: If a person may not place a harmful item right next to the border, the גמרא asks how the case of the משנה could ever come about.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if one may not place it right up against the border, how can you find such a case?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a practical question: if putting a harmful thing right by the neighbor's border is not allowed, how would we ever have the situation the משנה describes? This question sets up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה, and רבי יוסי's argument in it, picture harmful things sitting close to a neighbor's property. But the rule is that one may not place them there in the first place. So the גמרא needs a realistic case where they end up close together without anyone breaking the rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Placed close, right up against the border
How can you find it? In what real situation does this happen?

phrases.english: And if one may not place it close,
how can you find such a case?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי דְּלָא סָמֵיךְ, הֵיכִי מַשְׁכַּחַתְּ לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the discussion of the משנה about distancing harmful items, now asking how the case could happen at all.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A realistic scenario where harmful items sit near a neighbor's border without anyone breaking the rule against placing them there.

steps.title: רב פפא: The case is a buyer
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא answers that the משנה is talking about a לוקח, someone who bought part of a field where the items were already in place.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: It is talking about a buyer.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא gives the case: someone bought part of his neighbor's field, and the harmful thing and the thing that can be harmed were already there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the buyer did not put the item there himself, nobody broke the rule about placing harmful things close to the border. This explains how the two things could end up right next to each other.

keyTerms.meaning: A buyer, here someone who bought part of a neighbor's field

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
It is talking about a buyer.
phrases.notes: Picture someone buying half a field where the harmful item was already sitting near the new dividing line.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The case is a לוקח who bought land where the items were already near each other, so no one placed them there improperly.

steps.title: If it is a buyer, both opinions are hard to understand
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא attacks רב פפא's answer: if the buyer did nothing wrong, why do the רבנן make him move his item? And why does רבי יוסי disagree only about חרדל and not about משרה and ירק?
steps.simpleTranslation: If it is a buyer, what is the reason of the רבנן? And also, what is the reason of רבי יוסי? Even flax-water and vegetables should be the same!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises two challenges against the buyer explanation. One is aimed at the רבנן and one at רבי יוסי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: First, a buyer acted properly, so why should the רבנן require him to move his harmful item? Second, if רבי יוסי is lenient because the buyer did nothing wrong, that same reason should apply to משרה near ירק. So why does he argue only about חרדל and bees?

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?
And furthermore, which brings a second challenge
Water used for soaking flax, which harms nearby plants
Vegetables

phrases.english: If it is a buyer,
what is the reason of the Rabbis?
And furthermore, what is the reason of Rabbi Yosei?
Even flax-water and vegetables should be the same!
phrases.notes: This is the משנה's first case, which רבי יוסי does not argue about.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the buyer explanation of step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב פפא's explanation that the משנה is talking about a לוקח
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A buyer acted properly, so the רבנן have no clear reason to make him move. And if רבי יוסי is lenient for that reason, he should be lenient with משרה and ירק too, yet he argues only about חרדל.

steps.title: רבינא: The one who causes harm must move away
steps.stepSummary: רבינא explains the רבנן: the מזיק always has to distance himself, even if he did nothing wrong when the items ended up in place.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: The רבנן hold that the one who causes damage must distance himself.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא answers the first challenge. He explains why the רבנן make even an innocent buyer move his harmful item.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to the רבנן, it does not matter how the item came to be there. Whoever owns the thing that causes harm carries the responsibility to keep it away. That is why the buyer must move it.

keyTerms.meaning: They hold, this is their view
The one who causes the damage
To distance himself, to move his item away

phrases.english: Ravina said:
The Rabbis hold:
It is on the one who causes damage to distance himself.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the first part of the challenge in step 3, the question about the רבנן.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifies the underlying principle behind the רבנן's ruling
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A buyer who did nothing wrong should not have to move anything.
steps.terutzMaskana: The רבנן hold that the מזיק always bears the responsibility to distance, no matter how the situation came about.
steps.whyThisMatters: The rule על המזיק להרחיק את עצמו is a central principle in the laws of neighbors' damages.

steps.title: Then רבי יוסי should be lenient with flax-water too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא infers that רבי יוסי must hold the ניזק has to distance himself. But if so, he should be lenient with משרה and ירק as well, not only with חרדל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does this mean רבי יוסי holds the one being damaged must distance himself? If it is on the one being damaged, even flax-water and vegetables should be the same!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא takes רבינא's explanation one step further and applies it to רבי יוסי. This brings back the second challenge from step 3.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the רבנן say the מזיק must move away, it seems רבי יוסי, who disagrees, holds that the ניזק must move away. But that principle would apply to every case, including משרה near ירק. So why does רבי יוסי argue only about חרדל and bees?

keyTerms.meaning: By implication, which suggests that
The one who is being damaged

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רבי יוסי has already been shown to hold that the ניזק must move away. The גמרא is only testing that idea, and the problem it finds is what drives the next part of the סוגיא.

phrases.english: Does this imply that Rabbi Yosei holds:
It is on the one being damaged to distance himself?!
If it is on the one being damaged,
even flax-water and vegetables should be the same!

steps.triggerLanguage: מִכְּלָל דְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי סָבַר: עַל הַנִּיזָּק לְהַרְחִיק אֶת עַצְמוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a conclusion from רבינא's answer about רבי יוסי and uses it to bring back the second challenge of step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: The implied view of רבי יוסי that follows from רבינא's explanation
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If רבי יוסי holds that the ניזק must distance himself, that rule would apply to every case. Yet he argues only about חרדל and bees, not about משרה and ירק.

steps.title: רבי יוסי also holds the damager must move, but mustard and bees harm each other
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא withdraws the idea that רבי יוסי holds על הניזק. He agrees the מזיק must distance himself. He only argues about חרדל and bees because there each one harms the other, so neither is purely the מזיק.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבי יוסי also holds that the מזיק must move away. This is what he is telling the רבנן: your rule makes sense for flax-water and vegetables, because the water harms the vegetables and the vegetables do not harm the water. But mustard and bees both harm each other!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 5 by changing what it assumed about רבי יוסי. He holds על המזיק like the רבנן, and he only argues about mustard because it is a two-way case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 5 we assumed רבי יוסי holds על הניזק, so we asked why he isn't lenient about משרה too. Now the גמרא says he agrees about משרה and ירק, since there the damage goes only one way. With mustard and bees the damage goes both ways, so the simple rule of 'the מזיק moves' doesn't settle who has to move.

keyTerms.meaning: The burden is on the one who causes the damage (to move away)
It works out fine / that makes sense
Water used for soaking flax
Mustard plant
Each other

phrases.english: Rather, actually Rabbi Yosei also
holds that it is on the one who causes damage,
phrases.notes: He means the one causing damage is the one who has to move his item away.

phrases.aramaic: וְהָכִי קָאָמַר לְהוּ רַבִּי יוֹסֵי לְרַבָּנַן:
phrases.english: and this is what Rabbi Yosei is saying to the Rabbis:
It works out well for flax-soaking water and vegetables,
since these damage those,
and those do not damage these,
phrases.notes: The water ruins the vegetables, but the vegetables do nothing to the water.

phrases.english: but mustard and bees,
both of them damage each other!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לְעוֹלָם רַבִּי יוֹסֵי נָמֵי עַל הַמַּזִּיק סְבִירָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 5 by dropping its assumption that רבי יוסי holds על הניזק.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-defining the opinion: רבי יוסי holds על המזיק, and his disagreement comes from mutual damage.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוסי holds על הניזק, so he should be lenient about משרה and ירק too.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יוסי agrees the מזיק moves. Mustard and bees are different because each harms the other.

steps.title: The Rabbis reply that bees do not really harm mustard
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן reject רבי יוסי's claim that the harm goes both ways. Bees cannot hurt mustard: they won't find the seed, and if they eat the leaf it grows back. So the bees are not damaged by anything here except the mustard, and mustard is the only real מזיק.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן? They say bees do not harm mustard. If they go for the seed, they won't find it. If they eat the leaf, it grows back.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how the רבנן answer רבי יוסי's argument from the last step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי's whole point was that the damage goes both ways. The רבנן deny that the bees cause any real loss to the mustard. So, in their view, mustard and bees are a one-way case just like flax-water and vegetables.

keyTerms.meaning: The seed (of the mustard)
Leaf
It grows back again

phrases.english: And the Rabbis?
phrases.notes: The גמרא is asking: how would the רבנן answer רבי יוסי's point?

phrases.english: Bees do not damage mustard;
if it is the seed, they will not find it,
if it is the leaf, it grows back again.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבָּנַן – דְּבוֹרִים לְחַרְדָּל לָא מַזְּקִי לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the רבנן's answer to רבי יוסי's argument in step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Factual denial: there is no two-way damage.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Bees and mustard harm each other, so it is unclear who must move.
steps.terutzMaskana: Bees cause no lasting damage to mustard, so mustard is the only מזיק.

steps.title: Challenge: elsewhere רבי יוסי says each person may use his own property
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא attacks the idea that רבי יוסי holds על המזיק. In a later משנה, רבי יוסי says a tree owner does not have to cut down a tree near a neighbor's pit, even if the pit was there first. That means the ניזק must protect himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does רבי יוסי really hold that the מזיק must move away? But we learned that רבי יוסי says: even if the pit was there before the tree, the tree owner does not have to cut it down, because this one digs in his own land and that one plants in his own land!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer of step 6 by quoting a different משנה where רבי יוסי clearly does not make the מזיק move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the pit-and-tree case, the tree's roots damage the pit, so the tree owner is the מזיק. Yet רבי יוסי lets him keep the tree, because everyone may act in his own property. This shows that רבי יוסי holds על הניזק, which contradicts step 6.

keyTerms.meaning: But we learned in a משנה
Pit or cistern
Tree
He need not cut it down

phrases.english: And does Rabbi Yosei hold that it is on the one who causes damage
to distance himself?!
But we learned: Rabbi Yosei says:
phrases.notes: This is a משנה later in this פרק, on דף כה:.

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהַבּוֹר קוֹדֶמֶת לְאִילָן –
phrases.english: Even though the pit came before the tree,
he need not cut it down,
for this one digs within his own property,
and that one plants within his own property!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְסָבַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי עַל הַמַּזִּיק לְהַרְחִיק אֶת עַצְמוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the claim made in step 6 that רבי יוסי holds על המזיק.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in step 6 that רבי יוסי holds על המזיק.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the pit-and-tree משנה, רבי יוסי lets the מזיק (the tree owner) stay put, which shows he holds על הניזק.

steps.title: רבי יוסי holds the damaged party must move, but argues using the Rabbis' rule
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to the idea that רבי יוסי holds על הניזק. His argument here about חרדל is not his own view. He is debating the רבנן on their own terms.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבי יוסי really holds that the ניזק must move away, and he is speaking to the רבנן according to their own opinion.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from step 8 with a new way of reading רבי יוסי's words in our משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now both sources fit: רבי יוסי's real view is על הניזק, as in the pit-and-tree משנה. His comment about mustard and bees is a 'even by your rule' argument aimed at the רבנן. This also answers step 5's question, because his own view would indeed be lenient about משרה and ירק.

keyTerms.meaning: The burden is on the one being damaged (to move away)
According to their own words or opinion

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think רבי יוסי changed his opinion in the משנה. He is only arguing 'even according to you,' and his own view is that the ניזק must move.

phrases.english: Rather, actually Rabbi Yosei
holds that it is on the one being damaged,
and he is speaking to them according to the words of the Rabbis:

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לְעוֹלָם רַבִּי יוֹסֵי עַל הַנִּיזָּק סְבִירָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 8 by bringing back the step 5 view that רבי יוסי holds על הניזק.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוסי's mustard argument shows his own view, which would be על המזיק.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יוסי holds על הניזק. The mustard argument is only debating the רבנן on their terms.
steps.whyThisMatters: It fits רבי יוסי's opinion here together with his opinion in the pit-and-tree משנה, so he holds one consistent view.

steps.title: רבי יוסי's full argument spelled out
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי says: in my view the ניזק moves, so even flax-water need not be moved. But even by your rule, which only works for one-way damage like flax-water and vegetables, mustard and bees damage each other.
steps.simpleTranslation: In my view, the ניזק must move away, and even flax-water and vegetables would not have to be distanced. But according to you, who say the מזיק must move: that works for flax-water and vegetables, because one harms the other and not the reverse. But mustard and bees both harm each other!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא spells out word by word what רבי יוסי was really saying to the רבנן. It repeats the line from step 6, but now as an 'according to you' argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'תינח משרה וירקא' appear again, but their job has changed. In step 6 they showed רבי יוסי's own view. Here they are only his challenge to the רבנן's view, after he first states that his own rule is על הניזק.

keyTerms.meaning: According to me / in my view
According to you (plural)
To distance / move away

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוסי holds על הניזק, so the damaged party protects himself. The רבנן hold על המזיק. רבי יוסי's mustard-and-bees argument is only 'even according to you,' and the רבנן answer that bees don't really harm mustard.

phrases.aramaic: לְדִידִי, עַל הַנִּיזָּק לְהַרְחִיק אֶת עַצְמוֹ,
phrases.english: In my view, it is on the one being damaged to distance himself,
and even flax-soaking water and vegetables
do not need to be distanced;
but according to you, who say it is on the one who causes damage:
It works out well for flax-soaking water and vegetables,
since these damage those,
and those do not damage these,
but mustard and bees,
both of them damage each other!

steps.triggerLanguage: לְדִידִי, עַל הַנִּיזָּק לְהַרְחִיק אֶת עַצְמוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the 'according to their words' answer given in step 9.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי יוסי holds על הניזק, so even משרה need not be moved. His mustard-and-bees point is only a challenge to the רבנן's rule of על המזיק.

steps.title: The Rabbis reply that bees do not harm mustard
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן answer רבי יוסי's claim that the harm goes both ways. Bees do not damage mustard. They begin with the case of the seed.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן say: bees do not damage mustard. If you mean the seed...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the רבנן's answer to רבי יוסי's argument from Step 10, that mustard and bees damage each other. This line only opens their answer, and the sentence continues right after.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 10, רבי יוסי said that even by the רבנן's own rule, mustard and bees are a two-way case. The רבנן deny this by saying bees cannot really hurt mustard. If that is true, mustard is the only מזיק, and the normal rule applies: the one doing the damage must move away.

keyTerms.meaning: And the Rabbis: how the רבנן answer the point just made
They do not damage it
The seed (here, the mustard seed)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the גמרא is going back to the start of the argument. It is giving the רבנן's reply to רבי יוסי's 'even by your own rule' argument, using the same reasoning as before.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis (how do they answer?)
bees do not damage mustard;
if it is the seed –

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבָּנַן דְּבוֹרִים לְחַרְדָּל לָא מַזְּקִי לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי יוסי's argument in Step 10 that mustard and bees damage each other.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Factual denial: the harm only goes one way
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוסי says mustard and bees harm each other, so the mustard owner should not be the one forced to move.
steps.terutzMaskana: Bees do not hurt mustard, so mustard alone is the מזיק and has to move away.
